data.title: Studsvik Issues Special Class E Shares for Long-Term Incentive Programs
data.description:
Studsvik AB ( (SE:SVIK) ) just unveiled an announcement.

Studsvik AB has resolved to issue and immediately repurchase up to 7,500 Class E1–E6 2026 shares and up to 120,000 Class E7 2026 shares to support its long-term incentive programmes for board members and key employees. Danske Bank will subscribe to the new Class E shares at SEK 1 per share, after which Studsvik will repurchase them at the same price.

The Class E shares are structured specifically for these incentive schemes and may be reclassified into ordinary shares if predetermined share price conditions are met at the end of the programmes. Any Class E shares not reclassified will be redeemed by the company and carry no dividend rights, aligning management and board incentives with long-term shareholder value while limiting dilution and cash outflows.

More about Studsvik AB

Studsvik AB is a Sweden-based provider of advanced technical services to the global nuclear power industry. The company focuses on fuel and materials technology, reactor analysis software, decontamination and radiation protection, and technical platforms for handling, conditioning and reducing the volume of radioactive waste, and it operates with around 540 employees in six countries with shares listed on Nasdaq Stockholm.

With more than 75 years of experience in nuclear technology and radiological services, Studsvik serves utilities and operators across international markets. Its specialized offerings support safe, efficient and compliant nuclear power operations, underpinning the company’s positioning as a niche technology and service provider within the nuclear energy value chain.

The breadth of Studsvik’s portfolio, from software to waste management, allows it to participate in both operational support and long-term decommissioning activities. This diversified exposure within the nuclear segment provides recurring service demand and a degree of resilience tied to the regulated, long-horizon nature of nuclear power assets.

data.title: AcroMeta Eyes Strategic Move Into Ambient-Temperature Cell Logistics With Macro HRD Term Sheet
data.description:

data.title: LibertyStream Secures Term Sheet for Up to US$95 Million in Project Financing
data.description:
An announcement from LibertyStream Infrastructure Partners ( (TSE:LIB) ) is now available.

LibertyStream Infrastructure Partners has signed a non-binding term sheet with Endurance Finance Partners for a proposed project financing framework of up to US$95 million. The package envisages a delayed-draw senior secured construction credit facility to fund its Freedom 1 and Freedom 2 projects, alongside potential financing for future sites, with draws tied to certified construction milestones and a five-year maturity.

The initial US$45 million portion for Freedom 1 and Freedom 2 would carry an interest rate of 12.25% and include warrant issuance to Endurance equal to up to 10% of that facility, exercisable for seven years, with final warrant terms to be set in definitive agreements. The financing remains subject to due diligence, internal approvals, regulatory consents and execution of definitive agreements, so there is no assurance the facilities will be completed, but the framework underscores LibertyStream’s push to secure substantial capital for scaling its lithium projects and reinforces its positioning in the energy and infrastructure lending market.

data.title: Compass Pathways Advances Redefine PTSD Trial, Keeping Psychedelic Therapy Hopes Alive
data.description:
Compass Pathways Plc (CMPS) announced an update on their ongoing clinical study.

The Redefine Study is a late-stage trial run by COMPASS Pathways to test whether its COMP360 psilocybin therapy can ease post-traumatic stress disorder symptoms. The official goal is to measure how well the treatment works and how safe and tolerable it is, a key step toward possible regulatory review and future commercial use.

The study is testing COMP360, a synthetic form of psilocybin designed for medical use. It is given in controlled sessions with close monitoring and support, aiming to reduce severe PTSD symptoms that often do not respond well to standard drugs.

The trial uses a randomized, parallel-group design, meaning participants are split by chance into different dose groups and followed over time. It is double-blind with several parties masked, so neither patients nor study staff know which dose is given, keeping results more reliable.

Participants receive one of three COMP360 doses: 1 mg, 10 mg, or 25 mg of psilocybin. The 1 mg dose serves as an active comparator, while 10 mg and 25 mg are tested as experimental doses to find the level that balances efficacy and safety.

The study was first submitted on April 30, 2026, marking the formal launch of the program. The most recent update on September 3, 2026 signals that the protocol and recruitment status have been refreshed and that the study is actively managed.

Primary and final completion dates are not yet posted, which suggests this program is still in the early to mid stages of enrollment and follow-up. Investors should expect key data readouts to be several quarters away, with timelines subject to change as recruitment progresses.

For CMPS, this update reinforces its push beyond treatment-resistant depression into PTSD, a large and underserved market. Clear progress in a Phase 2b/3 setting may support long-term growth expectations and keep the stock on the radar of healthcare and biotech-focused funds.

Competitors working on psychedelic-assisted therapies, including players in psilocybin and MDMA, are also moving through late-stage trials, raising both competitive pressure and investor interest in the space. Positive signals from the Redefine Study could lift sentiment across the sector, while setbacks may weigh on valuations.

Overall, the recruiting status and recent update show that COMP360’s PTSD program is advancing and remains a core asset for COMPASS Pathways. The study is ongoing and updated, with more details available on the ClinicalTrials.gov portal.
